newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds rise, spreads tighten.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds rise, spreads tighten.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities rose Tuesday afternoon, supported by a large buyer of conventional securities early in the session, mortgage experts said.
There was moderate mortgage banker selling, and pass-through yield spreads to comparable Treasuries narrowed by a few thirty-seconds, they said.

"Mortgages tightened by about three ticks and there was huge buying," said one Ginnie trader at an investment bank in New York. He said over $1.5 billion was purchased in conventional issues on the day.
Other traders confirmed there was a substantial purchase of conventional 8.0 percent and 8.5 percent paper, but would not say who the buyer was.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent issues were up 5/32 at 99-25/32, yielding 96 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper and Freddie Mac issues were up 4/32 at 99-24/32 and 99-30/32, respectively.
The five-year note was up 5/32 at 6.48 percent, while the 10-year note was up 8/32 to yield 6.62 percent.
